_comment: Every key the Python generators put into a payload the app reads, and what
happens to it on the other side (#262).
Why this file exists: the app decodes only the fields someone remembered to
wire up. `stopped_reason` was written on every halt and read by nothing, and
because the write really did run it looked alive to every is-this-used check
(#257). The sweep that followed found eight more, including OCR's `other`,
which Claude was asked for on every program and which generate_blog has a
prompt slot for that always rendered '(none)'.
The rule this file enforces:
- the Python side's real key set, read from the source by
tests/bridge_payload_keys.py, must equal this file's key set exactly.
A key Python gains fails until somebody declares what happens to it.
- every key marked `swift` must be read on the Swift side, proved by
PostRollApp/Tests/BridgePayloadContractTests.swift.
- a key that is deliberately not read by Swift is marked `python_only`
WITH A REASON. There is no third state: an orphan cannot sit here
unexplained, which is the whole point.
Two kinds of Swift side. `model` names a Codable type, and the guard
populates it, encodes it, and decodes it back, so deleting a line from
init(from:) fails. `reader` names a function that pulls keys out of a
dictionary by hand, and the guard feeds that function a payload carrying
every declared key and asserts each one comes back out. Both prove the key
is READ, not merely mentioned: a reader that keeps values generically
(parsePreviewDayEntry keeps any string that is an existing file) satisfies
this by behaviour without naming a single key, which is the point.

week_result._what: One event week's captions and blog, written after every day so a kill keeps what finished.

week_timing._what: Per-phase durations, feeding the rolling-mean estimate on the generation screen.

run_progress._what: Which step a long run is on, polled by the app so a working run is distinguishable from a dead one.

day_caption._what: One day's caption, hashtags and alt text.

skipped_photos.python_only: generate_week hoists this onto the week payload's `warnings`, which is where the app reads it and where it can be shown per day. DayCaption deliberately does not carry a second copy: two homes for one fact is how it goes missing in exactly one direction (L83).

blog_output._what: The blog post, plus what the deterministic checks caught.

revised_caption._what: A caption after a plain-English revision request.

revised_blog._what: A blog post after a plain-English revision request.

swapped_blog._what: A blog post rewritten around a different set of photos.

retried_blog_repair._what: What a retry of the alt text repairs did, and the body it ended with (#1160). `retry` is not decoration: repairs are silent, so a retry that repaired nothing and one that never ran would otherwise read identically on the only surface reporting either.

ocr_result._what: Structured program data read off the scanned pages.

web_performers._what: Who was on stage, read off the event's own web page. A separate lookup from where to find them online.

handle_suggestions._what: Suggested social handles for named performers, searched for on the web.

piece_notes._what: A short programme note per work, looked up once so it is not paid for twice.

ocr_flags._what: Fields the OCR review flags as probably wrong, with where each one came from.

collage_candidates._what: Alternative collage layouts offered in the gallery, each reproducible from its seed.

insight_report._what: What the Instagram export says performed, and what to change about the voice.

flag_review._what: Claude's reply in the OCR correction conversation, plus any patch to apply.

media_result._what: The week's rendered graphics, keyed by day, plus per-day failures (errors, which block the export) and per-day notes (warnings, which do not) (#265).

media_day._what: One day's rendered assets. A mix of plain path strings and nested objects.

friday_clip_plan._what: Friday's clip selection: which clips, in what order, trimmed where.

friday_clip_selection._what: One clip inside the Friday plan, already renamed into Swift's field names.

ocr_performer._what: One performer inside ocr_result.performers. Its own entry because the contract used to check only that `performers` arrived, so a field renamed one level down went missing the way `other` did for years (#274).

ig_post._what: One post read out of the Meta export CSV.

insight_findings._what: The four pattern lists inside a findings track (feed_findings, story_findings).

insight_finding._what: One finding inside a pattern list. `id` is stamped by _assign_ids after this, so it is not part of the declared shape.

blog_finding._what: One deterministic blog check result inside blog_output.findings.

caption_finding._what: One deterministic caption check result inside day_caption.findings. The same shape as a blog finding, built by the same `finding_entry`, and it had no entry of its own until #1156: #1132 widened that shared builder with a `repair` field, so caption findings carry it at runtime with nothing verifying either side.

cover_result._what: A single day's regenerated cover image.

friday_override_result._what: What a manual Friday reel re-render did, including a title card that could not be applied.

swap_reel_audio._what: The result of swapping a reel's audio track without re-encoding video.

meta_import._what: Instagram posts parsed out of Meta's CSV export.

learn_suggestion._what: One brand-voice rule inferred from the edits Dan made to generated text.

account_numbers._what: One row per handle the automatic fetch asked Meta about, including the ones that failed, feeding AccountBook.merge and the collaborator ranking (#1002, #1004).

_manifests_comment: The other direction (#266). Above: keys Python WRITES and Swift reads.
Below: keys Python READS out of a manifest Swift built.
This direction is the more dangerous one. A result key Swift stops decoding
shows the wrong thing on screen. A manifest key Swift stops SENDING is
silently replaced by Python's own default, and generation carries on making
something subtly different: the wrong photos, the wrong crop, the wrong
posting preset, with nothing anywhere reporting a problem.
Each key says whether Swift always sends it or sends it conditionally.
`always` is asserted against a fully populated Event on the Swift side, so
dropping one fails. `conditional` states WHEN it is sent, and is not
asserted, because its absence is a legitimate state: what the entry buys is
that the condition is written down rather than inferred from a nil check.

week._what: Everything generate_week needs for one event's captions and blog.

caption_context_photos.conditional: Sent whenever Wednesday has photos. Thursday's caption falls back to representative selection without it, which costs a Claude call and picks differently.

week_day._what: One day's entry inside the week manifest's `days` dict.

post_type.conditional: Sent when the day has one set; Python infers it from the preset and photo count otherwise.

tag_handles.conditional: Sent when anyone is credited on the day, by handle.

name_mentions.conditional: Sent when anyone is credited by name rather than handle.

notes.conditional: Sent when Dan wrote observations for the day.

photo_tags.conditional: Sent for collage-carousel days where individual photos carry people tags.

clips_plan.conditional: Friday only, and only once a clip reel has been cut.

media._what: Everything generate_media needs to render the week's graphics.

pieces.conditional: Sent when the programme has works on it; drives the reel's audio mood tags.

media_day._what: One day's entry inside the media manifest's `days` dict.

raw_photo.conditional: Tuesday and Friday, when a before shot has been assigned.

edited_photo.conditional: Tuesday and Friday, when an after shot has been assigned.

bw_photo.conditional: Optional third treatment; its absence is a deliberate choice, not a failure.

screen_recording.conditional: Tuesday only, when a screen recording has been imported.

clips.conditional: Friday only, when video clips have been imported.

audio.conditional: Sent when Dan uploaded his own track for the day.

cover_source.conditional: Sent when a cover has already been picked, so the sticky gate reuses it instead of paying Claude again.

cell_layout.conditional: Wednesday only, when the collage frames have been adjusted by hand.

crop_offsets.conditional: Sent when any photo on the day has been panned or zoomed.

collage_seed.conditional: Sent when a specific collage layout has been chosen; random each run otherwise.

reel_seed.conditional: Sent when a specific reel layout has been chosen; random each run otherwise.

reel_style.conditional: Sent when the day overrides the default reel style.

scroll_duration.conditional: Thursday only; Python has its own default.

target_duration.conditional: Tuesday only; Python has its own default.

clip_duck_db.conditional: Friday only, how far clip audio sits under the music.

clip_audio_muted.conditional: Friday only, when clip audio is muted outright.

title_card_muted.conditional: Friday only, when the title card's audio is muted.

cover._what: A single day's cover-image regeneration. Friday only since #961 removed Thursday's cover.

override_source.conditional: Sent only when Dan picked the cover by hand, which skips the Claude call entirely.

clips_plan.conditional: Friday only, so frames can be re-extracted without recutting the reel.

friday_override._what: Re-rendering Friday's reel from Dan's manual clip edits.

pieces.conditional: Sent when the programme has works on it; drives the audio mood tags.

audio.conditional: Sent when Dan uploaded his own track.

duck_gain_db.conditional: Sent when the day overrides how far clip audio is ducked.

mute_clip_audio.conditional: Sent when clip audio is muted outright.

title_card_muted.conditional: Sent when Dan turned the title card off for this event.

reel_preview._what: The fast Thursday strip the per-photo crop editor opens, with no video encode.

seed.conditional: Sent when a specific reel layout has been chosen, so the editor shows the same arrangement the reel will use; random otherwise.

crop_offsets.conditional: Sent only when at least one photo has been panned or zoomed, so an untouched day sends nothing.

swap_reel_audio._what: Replacing a rendered reel's music without re-encoding the video.

caption_revision._what: Rewriting one day's caption from a plain-English instruction.

blog_revision._what: Rewriting the blog post from a plain-English instruction.

blog_photo_swap._what: Rewriting the blog around a different set of photos.

org.conditional: Sent only when the swap knows its event. The damage gate refuses a rewrite that drops the organisation name from the post.

photo_stamps.conditional: Sent only when the swap knows its event, and empty for every post written before #1130. What the alt text in the incoming body was written against: without it the swap has no record to compare each photograph against, every one reads as new, and it re-uploads and re-describes six good alt texts to change one picture.

program.conditional: Sent when the swap knows its event AND that event has OCR data, so a blog written for an event whose programme was never scanned still swaps photos.

venue.conditional: Sent only when the swap knows its event, which the caption review screen always does; the standalone path passes no event and Python defaults the venue to an empty string.

venue_context.conditional: Sent only when the swap knows its event. The damage gate needs it: measured on the stored events, the Battery Dance Festival event carries an EMPTY venue with its real one, Robert F. Wagner Jr. Park, only here, so a known set built from venue alone refuses Dan correcting the venue to its own name (#1137).

blog_repair_retry._what: Retrying the alt text repairs a blog repair pass could not finish (#1162).

event_id.conditional: Sent only when the retry knows its event, which both callers do. Which post this is, so the repair journal's records are shown against it and no other (#1162).

venue.conditional: Sent only when the retry knows its event. Prose context for the alt text being rewritten; Python defaults it to an empty string without one.

program.conditional: Sent when the retry knows its event AND that event has OCR data, so a blog whose programme was never scanned can still have its alt text retried.

analytics._what: Reading the Instagram export to find what performed.

learn_suggestion._what: Inferring a brand-voice rule from the edits Dan made to generated text.

account_numbers._what: The handles the automatic fetch should ask Meta about (#1004).

_siblings._what: Payload shapes with MORE THAN ONE producer, and what each producer must therefore emit. Each payload above is checked against its own entry; nothing compared the two paths that make the same shape, so a key carried by one and dropped by the other was invisible at both ends. #1008 added alt_text_photo_paths to the generation path and the revision dropped it silently; it was caught only because Swift happened to read the key (#1023). `missing_in` excuses a key one producer legitimately has nothing to put in, naming the producer that LACKS it and why, and tests/test_sibling_payloads_agree.py holds every excuse to still being true. Which entries are in a group is no longer only a list somebody wrote: any two entries whose declared keys overlap by half or more must be grouped here or declared under `_unrelated` (#1357).

a day caption._what: What a day's caption panel reads, however it was produced.

skipped_photos.why: The photographs too large or unsupported to upload, decided by partition_uploadable when the photos are STAGED. A revision works from an existing caption and stages nothing, so it has none to report rather than having lost them.

a blog post._what: What the blog panel reads, however it was produced: written, revised, or rewritten around a different set of photographs.

title.why: A swap rewrites the prose around different photographs and keeps the post it was given. CaptionWorkManager merges the swap into the blog already on the event rather than decoding a fresh one, so the title it holds is carried forward and sending one back would be a second answer to a question nobody asked (#1357).

a performer._what: One performer, however the app learned about them: read off the printed programme, or off the event's own web page.

a check result._what: One deterministic check that fired, wherever it fired. The blog panel and the caption panel read the same shape, and #1156 gave the caption side an entry of its own; they are grouped so the day one of them starts building its own entries rather than calling `finding_entry`, the two are compared key by key rather than each being checked against itself (#1023).

_unrelated._what: Pairs whose declared keys overlap enough for #1357's sweep to ask, and which are NOT one shape produced twice. Each says why, because a pair left undeclared and a pair declared with no reason read the same from here.

pairs.why: A programme note LOOKED UP for a work, against a piece READ OFF the printed programme. They share the words that name a work, which is why they overlap, and nothing else: one carries the movements printed in the programme, the other carries notes fetched from the web, and they decode into different Swift types with different readers.

Both are keyed by day with errors and warnings beside them, which is the shape every whole-week result takes, but one holds rendered GRAPHICS per day and the other holds CAPTIONS and the blog. A day's value in one is a list of image paths and in the other a caption object, so the readers cannot be interchanged.
